scenario_description: The provider's raw output cites evidence id 'E99', which was never shown to it (only E1 exists in this package). The real parse_and_validate must drop the fabricating observation and hypothesis entirely, strip the fabricated id, and record the fabrication in its own validation notes.

provenance.notes: The provider_response_text is a hand-constructed adversarial payload simulating a model that invents an evidence id -- this is the exact fabrication shape investigator_service.llm.validation.parse_and_validate's own module docstring describes defending against.

ground_truth_rationale: A human reviewer confirms: this EvidencePackage contains exactly one real item (E1); 'E99' does not exist anywhere in it or in build_prompts' own shown_evidence_ids. Any observation/hypothesis whose ONLY citation is 'E99' must therefore be entirely dropped -- Phase 5's own correction rounds #1/#2 establish this is never acceptable, even with evidence_ids=[] retained as a weaker signal.

input.provider_response_text: {"summary": "attacker-controlled summary text", "observations": [{"statement": "a fabricated factual claim", "evidence_ids": ["E99"]}], "hypotheses": [{"statement": "a fabricated hypothesis", "supporting_evidence_ids": ["E99"], "conflicting_evidence_ids": [], "supporting_context_ids": [], "conflicting_context_ids": [], "confidence": "high"}], "missing_evidence": [], "suggested_checks": []}

forbidden_outcomes: E99 appearing anywhere in the sanitized observations/hypotheses
the fabricating observation or hypothesis surviving with evidence_ids/supporting_evidence_ids=[] instead of being dropped entirely
